subject: Latency & 5xx/429 rate spike — impact to Blue Horizon analytic pipelines
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@bluehorizon.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spike and 429s across inference endpoints - immediate help needed

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing elevated latency and a burst of 5xx/429 responses across our inference calls to the /v1/generate endpoint beginning ~08:50 PDT. Impact: several downstream analytic jobs are timing out and backfilling is failing.

What we see so far:
- 08:50–09:05: sustained 95th pct latency from 400ms -> 2.1s
- 08:58–09:08: correlated 429 spikes for batched requests (sample attached)
- Some requests retrying from our side, causing cascading traffic.

Attached: request-sample.log, 500-429-excerpt.json (small samples). Please confirm whether this is an infrastructure regression or a model-serving degradation, and provide an ETA for mitigation. We're currently throttling consumer jobs but need a more durable fix.

Thanks,
Maria Garcia
Platform Ops — Blue Horizon Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@bluehorizon.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ops Team <ops@bluehorizon.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spike and 429s across inference endpoints - immediate help needed

Thanks for the signal and the samples, Maria. We're escalating now. Initial asks/next steps: 

1) Karthik / Markus: please triage runtime and routing in parallel. Check recent rollout/traffic shifts, kernel selection failures, and autoscaler activity.
2) Maria: can you share the HubSpot request id or job ids for the failing backfills? That will help us trace traces.
3) We'll open an incident on our status page and share a brief customer note within 30m.

Temporary mitigations we are considering (will confirm):
- Rapidly apply a transient global rate cap to client tokens from Blue Horizon to stabilize retries
- Route traffic to a lower-capacity but more stable model variant (lower token memory)
- Bypass a newly-introduced batching optimization if it's causing tail latencies

I'll post a running update in 20 minutes.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@bluehorizon.ai>, Ops Team <ops@bluehorizon.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spike and 429s across inference endpoints - immediate help needed

On it — quick triage notes:
- No recent customer-facing model rollout in the last 24h.
- Observed elevated tail latencies across a small subset of GPU hosts in us-west-2 starting ~08:48.
- Autoscaler triggered a burst of scale-ups which coincided with an increase in queueing. Possible cascading effect with our continuous batching window.

Immediate actions we're executing:
- Disable the new batching window tweak for affected host pool (rollback flag applied).
- Temporarily disable autoscaling for the dedicated pool serving Blue Horizon and pin capacity to current instance set to avoid noisy neighbor retries.
- Apply a per-token soft rate-limit (20% below observed peak) for the BH API key to curb client-side retries.

ETA for stabilization: 30–45 minutes after changes complete (I will update). If that doesn't reduce 5xx/429 within that window, we'll failover routing to the secondary region and open a canary to validate.

Karthik
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime

From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@bluehorizon.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@bluehorizon.ai>, Trevor <trevor@acme-datatech.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spike and 429s across inference endpoints - immediate help needed

Thanks — quick clarifications and more context:
- HubSpot job ids: BH-4821, BH-4825, BH-4829 (included in request-sample.log).
- The backfills that failed are time-sensitive (daily reporting window). If you can stabilize within 1 hour that's mission-critical.
- We are already implementing client-side exponential backoff, but the retries are queued by our orchestrator due to short timeout settings.

Attachment: request-sample.log (contains request ids and timestamps).

Appreciate the quick action.
— Maria

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@bluehorizon.ai>, Ops Team <ops@bluehorizon.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spike and 429s across inference endpoints - immediate help needed

Status update (10:10 PDT):
- Rolled back batching-window tweak at 09:40 — observed immediate reduction in 95th% tail on affected hosts.
- Autoscaler pinned at 09:42 for the customer pool: this stopped the scale burndown/scale-up loop and reduced queue growth.
- Applied per-key soft rate limit at 09:50; 429s dropped ~62% in the next 8 minutes.

Remaining work / next steps:
- Continue monitoring for the next 60 minutes for reoccurrence.
- If stable, plan a controlled re-enable of batching with smaller window and metrics gating.
- Prepare a customer-facing status update and propose a 15% credit for uptime impact while we complete post-incident RCA.

ETA to confirmed stability: 30 minutes (monitoring).

Markus
Director, Platform Reliability

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@bluehorizon.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Customer impact summary and proposed comms — Blue Horizon (inc: INC-3456)

Team, final summary and ask for approval:

Incident summary:
- Window: 08:48–10:05 PDT on 2027-05-10
- Impact: elevated 95th pct latency and a transient surge of 5xx/429 responses that caused job timeouts for Blue Horizon daily backfills.
- Root cause (preliminary): interaction between a recent batching-window optimization and autoscaler churn causing queueing on a subset of hosts. Full RCA pending.

Customer impact/status:
- Blue Horizon saw failures in three backfill jobs (BH-4821/4825/4829); they need confirmed re-runs but core service stabilized.
- Markus' mitigation (rollback batching, pin autoscaler, per-key rate limit) reduced 429s by ~62% and tail latency improved; monitoring window to complete.

Proposed customer-facing message (short):
"We rolled back a recent batching optimization and applied targeted capacity controls which stabilized request latency and reduced error rates. We will follow up with an RCA and are offering a 15% service credit for the impacted billing period. Affected jobs can be re-run; Redwood will provide priority assistance for scheduling."

Approvals needed: 1) Confirm 15% credit for Blue Horizon (finance ok?) 2) Sign-off on status page copy above.

Attachments: status-draft.md (customer note + status page snippet).

Vanessa
Head of Customer Reliability
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
